headings.title: One bounded selection attempt per semantic input

html:
Tool discovery

native/catalog.py owns the CORE set and built-in control declarations. Core candidates include Shell/Python, Files, HTTP, Web, Artifacts, Agent Introspection, Task Scratchpad (KV), Memory put/get/search and schedule creation/inspection. Being in CORE determines initial advertisement when permitted and available; it does not make every candidate mandatory. Agent Introspection, Task Context, KV, Memory and Shell are always selected for new requests in both Automatic and Manual. Their Skill/tool exclusions are normalized away, and Auto cannot omit them from its accepted selection. Memory and Shell still obey workflow restrictions and current availability. Advisory mode permits local Memory and KV but excludes external Shell execution. Required internal tools, including all five KV tools, remain available inside workflow fences and focused tool views, including in saved runs. Execution permission checks still apply. Optional candidates require capability selection and current availability. Controls cover task organization, discovery, scoped context/results, jobs/events/activity waits, user interaction and completion. Shell sequencing, dependency scheduling and parallel tool families add declarations when their own conditions apply. The initial schema set therefore depends on the run's configuration and prerequisites.

Automatic selection also retains file.read whenever the accepted tool ceiling permits it. The model can read known files without selecting the whole Files skill; other Files tools still require selection or discovery. File read obeys explicit exclusions, workflow and Advisory restrictions, and Gateway availability.

For example, an Auto selection of Files for “check pending changes in this repository” also includes Memory and Shell, allowing the Agent to run git status. Discovery cannot widen the accepted authority ceiling. Existing runs retain their saved selection; use a new request after updating to adopt the new always-selected Skills.

An empty discover_tools call lists registered skills and tools, including unavailable entries with reasons, without exposing every full schema. {"skill_ids":["database"]} adds that family's available schemas to subsequent model requests. Use the exact lowercase skill IDs returned by discovery; display titles are not IDs. Exact capability_ids can select individual tools. Unknown or forbidden entries fail atomically. Unavailable requests return prerequisite information without advertising an unusable schema. Discovery executes nothing and grants no authorization.

Canonical tool IDs contain a dot. The OpenAI-compatible function-name wire format uses __: shell.command is sent as shell__command. Receipts and documentation use canonical dotted IDs. Only the visible schemas may be called.

Use skill_ids for families such as schedule, capability_ids for exact tool IDs such as schedule.inspect, and section_ids only for returned API section IDs. Invalid selections return an actionable retry discovery call to the model. A recognized, permitted family uses skill_ids; otherwise the retry lists the catalog. The failed selection advertises no tools and does not execute an adapter. Recovery never creates aliases or expands capability policy. Discovery failures establish no facts about the requested data: an unavailable inspection cannot prove a zero count.

Capability awareness, activation and grants

Concept Responsibility
Capability Manifest What the Agent knows exists: installed, user-routable Skills and source-owned routing summaries.
Capability Policy / frozen ceiling What this accepted run may expose, within its captured upstream restrictions.
Active projection The Skills and tools selected for the current semantic request.
Tool discovery Concrete schemas and entry tools from the active projection.
Task resource grant An explicit user decision bound to displayed resources and this task; saved capability and permission policies remain unchanged.
Permission Policy Whether a concrete operation is allowed, requires approval, or is denied.
Credentials / authentication Whether the provider or resource can actually be accessed.
Activity Trace Durable events explaining each capability transition.

Automatic mode places a versioned, digested Manifest in stable Task State. It contains canonical Skill IDs, display names, selection modes and one-line summaries from the registry. Dependency-only Skills are omitted. Building it does not inspect credentials, probe providers or include tool schemas. The initial selector still uses the smaller candidate catalog inside the accepted ceiling. Task Contract compilation continues to provide that initial selection when enabled; no separate selector call is added.

During the request, the Agent can call discover_tools(skill_ids=["docker"]) after, for example, reading a Compose file. If Docker is inside the frozen ceiling, the runtime commits a new selection epoch containing the prior active set plus Docker and its permitted dependencies, rebinds the scoped catalog, then returns entry-tool discovery. This uses no helper model and needs no user prompt. A later request for database or http can grow the same projection. Already-active Skills produce an audited no-op. At the next semantic user input, normal selection can contract the projection again.

Activation accepts at most eight exact canonical Skill IDs per discovery request. Mixed requests are atomic: one blocked Skill prevents partial activation. Section IDs and tool IDs discover only within the current projection; they cannot activate a Skill. Discover newly needed Skills separately before selecting sections or exact tools. Direct requests for dependency-only Skills fail. An inactive explicit_only Skill requires a correlated user trigger. Manual mode retains its existing discovery behavior.

For an excluded Skill such as GitHub, discovery enters the task resource-consent path in native/resource_access.py. It freezes server-resolved resource identities and opens the existing permission card through native/authority_control.py, without another model decision. Tool exposure does not itself grant access. discover_resources and request_resource_access use the same authority lifecycle for supported individual resources and explicitly requested collections.

The structured decision must include the exact authority_request_id, displayed operation_id and authority_decision (allow or deny). The writer checks task, semantic input, authority, resource identities and policy revisions. A stale or changed request conflicts instead of acquiring broader consent. Allow records the frozen grant and creates a child continuation with a new immutable tool ceiling; the parent's ceiling and saved policies remain unchanged. The child retains the original user policy and binds a live resource predicate for each invocation. Denial preserves existing authority and suppresses the same unchanged request.

A grant covers the displayed resource's supported operations for this task. It does not confer access to independently restricted resources: copying between two locations, for example, requires both boundaries to match. Credentials, provider/OS permissions, implementation availability and operation validation still apply. The execution engine revalidates matching task consent at dispatch; a policy or identity change can invalidate it. Grants survive supported continuations of the same task but do not become conversation defaults or transfer to another task or scheduled occurrence. See the maintained resource-consent guide for discovery examples and scope details.

Older pending capability cards retain their original displayed scope. Their compatibility path in native/capability_grants.py can update conversation eligibility, compare both inherited scope revisions and create the corresponding child continuation. This is recovery behavior for old requests; newly issued Skill and resource requests use task-only consent. Tests using tests/legacy_capability_fixtures.py deliberately emulate that older issuance and must not be treated as evidence that new grants edit conversation settings.

Activation epochs, authority decisions and parent/child records commit with native state. Continuation workers repair task and UI projections after restart; exact request identities prevent duplicate approval. Stop, pause and newer semantic input retain their normal fences. See Activity.

Accepting the initial tool projection

Selection narrows a server-owned capability ceiling to a useful working set. It does not execute the selected tools or acquire their credentials. The data path joins capability_selection.py with the native selector:

flowchart LR Policy[Accepted capability policy and upstream restrictions] --> Ceiling[Frozen tool ceiling and grant provenance] Registry[Source-owned registry metadata] --> Ceiling Ceiling --> Catalog[Compact candidate Skill catalog] Request[Semantic user input and accepted attachment fingerprint] --> Identity[Selection source digest] Catalog --> Input[Bounded request context and routing summaries] Identity --> Input Memory[Accepted helper memory projection] --> Input Input --> Hint[Compiler hint or effect-free selector response] Hint --> Project[Validate IDs and add required, Always and permitted dependency tools] Ceiling --> Project Project --> Epoch[Accepted immutable selection epoch within ceiling] Epoch --> Tools[Rebuilt catalog and advertised schemas] Tools --> Dispatch[Later ordinary authorization and execution]

The accepted ceiling contains a digest, per-Skill tools/dependencies and provenance. The candidate catalog omits dependency-only Skills. Always-tool selection adds its owner's guidance without selecting every sibling tool; final tool expansion always intersects the ceiling. Current implementation availability is a separate live projection and can change without rewriting an accepted epoch.

One bounded selection attempt per semantic input

sequenceDiagram participant R as Owned request preparation participant S as Native compilation session participant H as Routed helper model participant C as Accepted request context participant K as Run catalog R->>R: Compare current selection with semantic source digest alt Manual mode or current accepted selection R->>K: Reuse accepted projection as needed else Automatic mode needs selection alt Combined Task Contract hint is expected R->>S: Accept hint in the existing compiler transaction Note over R,S: Missing hint in retained compiler state degrades without a new helper call else Standalone selector R->>S: Save reserved attempt and transport-start state before calling S->>H: Ask for strict Skill selection within captured catalog opt One omitted accepted-context page is requested H-->>S: Context-read request S->>C: Read bounded accepted page C-->>S: Requested context data S->>H: Return page within the same two-call budget end H-->>S: Final selection hint or inference failure end S->>S: Check cancellation, acceptance fence and unchanged source digest S->>S: Commit selection epoch or bounded degraded fallback S->>K: Rebind tools, discovery and Skill instructions S->>S: Publish queued trace events after acceptance end

The compiler path normally accepts its hint in the existing Task Contract transaction. The standalone helper saves its reservation before transport, permits at most one accepted-context read plus final selection, and limits each output to the smaller of 512 tokens and that model's output allowance. Input capacity is checked for the actual routed model, including transport fallback.

An already reserved attempt recovered for the same source digest becomes degraded instead of making another hidden helper request. Invalid or unavailable selector output falls back to the accepted ceiling; it cannot expand authority. A stale response is discarded. Cancellation and context-capacity/publication failures retain their own stopping behavior rather than proceeding into business tools.

Accepted epochs retain their source/ceiling/catalog digests and monotonically increasing identity. Resume validates and restores the saved projection, applying only explicit core-tool migrations. A genuinely changed semantic user input may select a new projection. Discovery activation later grows it under the existing bounded activation contract above, without another selector model call.

Large API skills

For a skill with entry_tool_ids, discovering its skill_id advertises those entries and returns root section metadata. The general catalog lists entry metadata for that skill instead of every raw endpoint. For example:

{"skill_ids":["proxmox"]}

This yields the four Proxmox domain tools plus root sections. Explore a source API section with:

{"section_ids":["proxmox.nodes.node.qemu.vmid.status"]}

The response contains direct tools and child metadata; it does not expand all descendants. Discovering another raw slice replaces that large skill's prior raw advertisements while retaining entry tools. Unknown section IDs return unknown_section; an excluded skill remains inaccessible. Exact tool discovery still respects the same policy. Existing small skills retain full-family discovery.

Proxmox is disabled by default. An accepted typed Proxmox @parameter can promote its already-allowed entry tools into the initial request, but cannot change the capability selection or approval requirements. See Proxmox VE.

Use the generated Tool and Skill Reference for the current registration list. A static count in this page would drift from the registry and would not describe the schemas available to a particular run.

The served generated Tool and Skill Reference constructs the current source-owned registry without executing tools. Availability metadata describes prerequisites; credential requirements remain explicit and remote health is not inferred. scripts/v55_final_catalog.py remains a historical validation/schema-evidence utility, outside mandatory product-source documentation.

Email is enabled by product default, subject to explicit selections and exclusions. An accepted email_smtp parameter promotes email.accounts, email.connect, email.connection_status, email.test_connection and email.send only within the accepted envelope. Sending remains a confirmed write. Configuration and authorization prerequisites do not silently switch to Gmail or controller-local SMTP.

Desktop is disabled by default. Its three entry tools and applications/processes/windows sections use the same bounded discovery contract. Each tool checks its exact captured Gateway sub-capability; missing window support does not disable processes. See Desktop.

Clipboard is disabled by default. Its inspect/read-text entry tools and text/files/image sections use negotiated format tags on the selected Gateway. Enabling it never reads clipboard content. See Current clipboard.

Screen is disabled by default. Its five explicit observation tools use independent negotiated metadata/capture/OCR tags. Discovery and metadata-only context never capture pixels. See Screen capture, OCR and context.

Browser is disabled by default. Its four entry tools and six sections use the same bounded discovery contract. The selected Gateway advertises managed, explicit-CDP and file capabilities independently. The status tool remains available to explain missing optional prerequisites. See Browser automation.

Web Research is an optional guidance Skill sharing only web.search and web.read. Its compact manifest/routing entry uses the existing selector; Browser remains a separate activation/grant. See Web Research.

Desktop UI is optional and sectioned. Discover ui for status, snapshot, find and focused_element; semantic actions, input and waits are available through sections. Selected Gateway tags distinguish accessibility, keyboard, pointer and drag support. See Desktop UI automation.

GitHub is optional and disabled by default. Its five entry tools expose local accounts, connection verification, repository resolution, issues and PR inspection; eleven sections provide bounded access to provider operations. A typed github_account promotes only already-permitted entries. See GitHub.

Matching consent to an invocation

resource_access.py owns the source binding catalog and live invocation matcher. It compiles supported/delegated operations from the registered resource definitions, retaining fixed CRUD arguments, identity selectors, execution targets and tool-contract digests. Only explicitly reviewed skill families participate. A changed binding must match the existing source review manifest; coverage reporting does not approve changes automatically. Cached bindings are keyed by registry authorization revision and returned as detached copies.

A discovered resource reference is a stable digest of its identity and contract, not a bearer credential. Object requests need a complete identity alternative; collections must be explicit. Declared host, account, profile, conversation and Gateway boundaries remain part of matching. An identity field omitted by the invocation is not a wildcard, and conflicting aliases do not select whichever value would happen to pass. Generated Proxmox endpoint paths substitute and encode exact declared parameters without contacting the provider.

The native run owner binds an in-process AccessSession to its execution context. A caller-supplied JSON object cannot substitute for that instance. Each match checks the native attempt, task ownership, live policy stamp, resource reference and current identity/contract revisions. Policy or account/Gateway identity changes can invalidate a previously accepted grant; ordinary display-label changes and resource content are not themselves the policy stamp.

Grant or operation Matching boundary
Skill Covers the skill's supported tool surface; independent host/account/file restrictions still apply.
Exact object Requires its declared identity and fixed operation discriminators.
Explicit path collection Permits the exact normalized path and separator-bounded descendants, not sibling name prefixes.
File copy/move/diff/patch Every operand must be covered, possibly by separate file grants. Unified-diff targets are parsed before matching.
Cross-Gateway copy Source must match file.read on the selected source Gateway and destination must match file.write on the selected destination Gateway.
Gateway execution Must stay within captured base targets, explicitly selected user targets or a valid Gateway grant for this attempt.

Path matching uses the selected Gateway's Windows or POSIX dialect. Relative paths need an absolute captured working root; unresolved ~, $, parent traversal and NUL characters are rejected. This normalization is lexical: the Gateway still resolves physical paths and enforces the forwarded task scope. Path grants reject follow_symlinks; exact object grants do not authorize recursive expansion or parent creation. Artifact-namespace preparation belongs to its existing owner and can perform Gateway setup; a failed/unresolved preflight is not a new grant.

A matching invocation can receive a detached authorization receipt containing task, grant and exact invocation identities. That receipt is diagnostic evidence, not an input credential. Invocation-local capability changes do not edit saved policies. When creating separate work, new_task_context removes borrowed grant/attempt state and restores the configured base context, preventing task consent from becoming a schedule or another task's authority.

Binding tests exercise exact identities, alias conflicts, complete operands, policy revisions and physical file-scope enforcement with local/fake providers. Task-consent tests exercise the existing HTTP permission card and same-task continuation boundary.
